newsitem.title: USA: CAIS rolls out new Internet access technology.
newsitem.headline: CAIS rolls out new Internet access technology.

text.p: CAIS Internet, a division of CGX Communications, said Tuesday it was rolling out a new high-speed Internet access technology that uses existing telephone lines.

The new technology, called OverVoice, lets consumers use their telephone wiring for a continuous connection to the Internet at speeds ranging from 1.54 megabits per second (Mbps) up to 10 Mbps. Initially, OverVoice customers will have Internet access at 1.54 Mbps, the company said.

Consumers can use the phone while surfing the Web. They also get continuous Internet access without having to dial in. The technology adapts the Ethernet standard used for personal computer Local Area Networks (LANs) to existing telephone wiring, the company said.

The new service is now available at the Arlington Courthouse Plaza Apartments in Arlington, Virginia. The Washington Marriott hotel has the service in its meeting rooms and plans to expand to selected guest rooms shortly, the company said.
After a six-month trial, the Internet service in Arlington is expected to cost between $40 and $50 per month.
The company said consumers need only a standard Ethernet card found at a retail store for their computer to get the OverVoice service.

CAIS said it is targeting multi-dwelling units and is seeking distribution and licensing agreements with commercial real estate developers, and owners and operators of apartments, condominiums, and hotels, as well as schools, other Internet Service Providers, and value added resellers.
CGX Communications, which acquired CAIS Internet last year, provides first-tier Internet access, long distance, and operator services.
